prompt: A dynamic array doubles its capacity whenever it fills. Starting empty, what is the amortized time per append over $n$ appends, assuming a copy or write costs $\Theta(1)$?

answers.explanation: The copied capacities form a geometric series $1+2+4+\cdots=O(n)$. Together with $n$ writes, the total cost is $\Theta(n)$, or $\Theta(1)$ per append.
The total work is linear, not cubic as this per-operation bound would imply.
Doubling capacity makes resizing infrequent; it does not cause exponential total copying.

answers.text: There is no finite amortized bound.
answers.explanation: Summing the geometric series gives a finite linear total cost.
A single resizing append can be linear, but that is a worst-case individual cost, not the amortized cost.
The total cost is linear, which yields a constant cost per append.
This overcounts copying: an old capacity is copied only when that capacity fills.
There are logarithmically many resizes, but the total copied elements form a geometric sum, not n times the number of resizes.
Every append performs at least one write; its amortized cost cannot decrease below a constant.

answers.text: Constant amortized time only if the append values are random.
answers.explanation: The bound holds for every sequence of append values; it is not a distributional average.
